decoder.coverage_rule: Every word is one of three things. `scalar`: named from the R4000/MIPS III table that p44 and p47 name for the SU — the manual does not tabulate the encoding, so each such entry is labelled `family`, not `cited`. `vector`: identified as a COP2 vector-unit instruction with its fields reported raw, its mnemonic null, and listed in `unreadable`. `unreadable`: named in no document this repository holds. Nothing is imported from another architecture's table, and no DMEM offset, SP register or command opcode acquires a name.

table_defects: the transpose group lists `0x01 swv` while the scalar group lists `0x01 lsv/ssv`: one opcode cannot be both, so one of the two rows mis-states it. No word in this program uses the transpose group, so nothing here depends on which
the computational table omits `funct 0x11`, which this program uses twice; it is left unnamed and listed rather than guessed at
external_sources.why: The local manual tabulates no RSP encoding — it delegates the SU to the R4000 manual by name (p44, p47) and says nothing about the vector unit's function codes. M223 therefore left all 254 vector words unnamed. M224 narrowed the rule rather than the refusal: an external table may be *used as a cited source* — attributed, no text reproduced, every consequence re-measured against the cartridge — which is what this project already does for OpenBiohazard2 (MIT) and libdragon (Unlicense). See docs/THIRD_PARTY.md 4b.

evidence.measurement: IMEM 0x000-0x024 is a status poll and nothing else: `mfc0 a2,<cop0 11>` / `andi a1,a2,1` / `beq a1,zero,0x028` / `andi a1,a2,0x100` / `beq a1,zero,0x028`, then a spin `mfc0 a1,<cop0 11>` / `andi a1,a1,0x100` / `bgtz a1,0x018`, and only then does the program touch anything (0x028 is the first vector instruction). 23 of the program's 24 COP0 moves are in its first 0x3d0 bytes, and 24 words are COP0 moves.
evidence.reading: a program that begins by polling a hardware status word and issuing no work before it is reachable is ucode driven by a task, not a data table: the wait has to be for the engine that started it. Register 11 is called the RSP status register by N64 documentation this repository does not hold — the name is recorded as coming from outside this repository's authority, the number and the poll are measured, and nothing downstream depends on the name.
evidence.status: measured; register name outside local authority

evidence.measurement: the task block carries four pointer+size pairs — +0x08/+0x0c, +0x10/+0x14, +0x18/+0x1c, +0x30/+0x34 — and the +0x10/+0x14 pair names this blob (0x800b2700, 0x1000). Each value was folded out of the store that writes it, not quoted.
evidence.reading: the block is a task header in the p137 sense: a structure the CPU fills and hands over with a pointer to the microcode and a pointer to the data to process.

evidence.measurement: the +0x08/+0x0c pair names 0x80028a80 with size 0xd0 (= 0x80028b50-0x80028a80), and the bytes there are CPU-shaped MIPS: `lw v1,0(s0)`, `sw v0,0x14(v1)`, `jalr v0`, and a `jr ra` at 0x80028b14 whose delay slot is `addiu sp,sp,0x28`. This project's corpus has FUN_80028b1c starting 0x9c bytes later, so the 0xd0 extent straddles a function boundary.
evidence.reading: the manual gives that pair the *boot microcode* role — RSP code the R4300 DMAs into IMEM before the task microcode (p137) — and these bytes are not RSP code. Either the pair carries something else in this cartridge, or the block is not the OSTask of p137. Recorded against both candidates rather than smoothed.

evidence.measurement: the declared size is 0x1000 = all of IMEM (p44), but the program is 0xf40 bytes: the corpus's own function FUN_800b3640 begins at 0x800b3640, 0xc0 bytes before the window ends, and the RSP program's last exit is 0xf34 `jr t0` (delay 0xf38, `nop` fill 0xf3c).
evidence.reading: the size field is IMEM's capacity, not the code's length: the declared 0x1000 overruns the program by 0xc0 bytes into the next CPU function. A task that DMAs 0x1000 bytes into IMEM therefore loads the whole program plus 0xc0 bytes of CPU code that no exit reaches. The overrun is recorded, not corrected.

evidence.measurement: IMEM 0x02c-0x030 (`lw a0,0x30(r1)` and `lw v1,0x34(r1)`) read DMEM 0x30 and 0x34 — the same two offsets the CPU writes at 0x800a2ed0/0x800a2ed4 as the work-list pointer and its count — before the program has written anything to DMEM.
evidence.reading: the block at 0x80143c60 is in DMEM when the program starts, which is the mechanism p137 describes (the R4300 DMAs the task header into DMEM, sets PC to 0). It also means the program assumes r1 holds zero at entry, and nothing in this repository establishes what the RSP's general registers hold when a task starts — the manual lists the boot ucode, the task header, PC and the halt status and no register state (p137). The assumption is recorded; it is not explained.

evidence.measurement: 24 COP0 moves: registers [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 7] are written, registers [5, 6, 7, 11] are read. Five blocks repeat one shape — write three registers carrying data, then poll a fourth, and clear register 7 with `mtc0 zero` — at 0x350, 0x384, 0x3b4 and 0x228-0x3c8.
evidence.reading: the shape is one DMA primitive copied: a source, a destination and a length are written and a busy flag is polled. Which number is which is *not* claimed — no local document maps the SP registers — so the copy's direction stays unresolved even though the idiom is measured.

evidence.measurement: 106 words address DMEM by 16-bit displacement, across 42 distinct offsets from 0x000 to 0xd5c. No offset is named.
evidence.reading: the program's whole interface with the CPU is DMEM plus DMA, and the layout it builds there is the ucode's own. Nothing on the CPU side mirrors it, so no field of it can be matched against a documented ABI from inside this repository.

evidence.measurement: the +0x18 pair names 0x80136b50 with size 0x800, and no other instruction in stage-2 names that address — 0 references, scanned as a `lui 0x8013` + `addiu 0x6b50` pair and as a literal. Its last 0x5c0 bytes run past the image's end at 0x80136d90.
evidence.reading: the region the ucode is handed as data is never touched by the CPU: it is either the ucode's own DMA target or its scratch, and which one is `rsp_only`.

evidence.measurement: the program's only four `lui` constants are .
evidence.reading: the last 0xc0 bytes build RDRAM addresses in code instead of taking them from a pointer, and 0x8016xxxx sits above this image's end. The scheme the manual describes is that the task header carries the pointer to the data to process (p137), so a hard-coded RDRAM address is a departure from it. It does not by itself name the ucode's author.

evidence.measurement: the first `what_would_decide` item was an RSP encoding table this repository could cite. It arrived in M224 and was applied in M225: 252 of the 254 vector words now carry a cited mnemonic, and the census says the units run a 16-bit fixed-point multiply-accumulate pipeline (%d multiply, %d multiply-accumulate, %d accumulator reads) in five cited formats. The same milestone measured the call structure: no computed transfer anywhere, every `jal` direct, and no load that selects a target.
evidence.reading: the table did not make this ucode's identity decidable, and it decided *against* the first candidate's predicted shape rather than for it: the ABI that candidate describes predicts a command list the ucode dispatches on, and this program has no dispatch of any kind. What the table bought is the arithmetic — the mixer is a fixed-point MAC pipeline — which is a description of the units, not a name for the ucode.

what_would_decide: ANSWERED (M224/M225): an RSP encoding table was cited, the 254 vector words are named and the COP0 registers have names and directions. It did not make the identity decidable — the jal fan-out did not read as a command switch, because there is no computed transfer at all (E8)
a CPU-side consumer of the 0x800 bytes at 0x80136b50 (E6): what the ucode is expected to write there is an ABI fingerprint
an independent copy of the same ucode from another N64 title: byte equality would settle provenance without a table

evidence: the corpus declares a CPU function at 0x800b3640: src/stage2/FUN_800b3640.c
the RSP program's last exit is 0xf34 `jr t0` with its delay slot at 0xf38, followed by a `nop` fill at 0xf3c; the next word is the CPU function's body

the words from 0xf40 build a KSEG0 address (`lui v0,0x8016` + `addiu v0,v0,-0x74e0` = 0x80158b20) and load/store through it — an RSP load cannot name RDRAM (p139: the RSP software can only access DMEM), so these are not RSP instructions

the arithmetic agrees with the corpus body: FUN_800b3640 walks a 0x1228-stride table and compares +0x1224 against _DAT_8015af70 (0x800b3640:22-27), and the words here carry `addiu a0,a0,0x1228` and `lw v0,0x1224(a0)`
foreign.not_decoded_as: program words: they are listed in no function, contribute to no jump target and to no DMEM statistic

jump_encoding.note: counted over RSP words only. The one jump in the CPU tail (0xfa8 `j`, raw target 0xb3650 = 0x800b3650) is excluded and is itself a CPU jump, which corroborates where the program ends
jump_encoding.rule: jal and j carry an absolute IMEM offset, not a PC-relative one: the RSP program counter is 12 bits because IMEM is 4 KB (p44), so the target is (instr_index << 2) & 0xFFF. Measured, not assumed: all 49 jump fields in the program have raw instr_index<<2 inside one 4 KB page (0x0400112c-0x04001eb4), so the page bits are constant and carry no target information; unmasked, every one of the 49 lies outside a 4 KB IMEM. Branches are the opposite: PC + 4 + (offset<<2), also truncated to IMEM.

rsp_only.cpu_evidence: none — measured by scanning every stage-2 instruction that touches the task's own structures
rsp_only.what: the DMEM layout the ucode builds
rsp_only.why: the program's only data addressing is a 16-bit DMEM displacement (106 words, 42 distinct, 0x000-0xd5c). The CPU writes no structure the ucode reads by name, so every offset is decided inside the RSP and nothing on the CPU side can be cited for it

rsp_only.cpu_evidence: none — the CPU never writes a vector register
rsp_only.what: what the vector unit's arithmetic computes
rsp_only.why: since M224 the 254 words are *named* — 252 of them from a cited table, 2 refused because it has no row for their function code — but a name is not a meaning. `vmadh v2,v1,v0` says which instruction runs, not which signal it filters, and the mixer's structure is in the accumulator's use, which no document here describes

rsp_only.cpu_evidence: the task field that names it, and nothing else
rsp_only.what: the meaning of the 0x800 bytes at 0x80136b50 (task+0x18)
rsp_only.why: no stage-2 instruction reads or writes that address (0 references) and its tail runs past the image. Whether the ucode treats it as input or scratch is decided only by the RSP

rsp_only.cpu_evidence: src/stage2/FUN_800a4d30.c writes the list base; the list's contents come from the voice path (M222), which stops at this same boundary
rsp_only.what: the command format the ucode dispatches on

rsp_only.what: whether the ucode is correct, or what it sounds like
rsp_only.why: this tool decodes instructions. Nothing here has been executed, so no claim is made that the program runs, terminates, or mixes

task.address_rule: A stage-2 address is folded from the instructions that write the register before the store: `lui rt,imm16` sets rt = imm16 << 16, `addiu rt,rt,imm16` / `ori rt,rt,imm16` adds the low half, and `subu` folds when both halves are known. The fold records the instructions it used and --check re-derives it; no word of stage-2 contains the literal 0x800b2700 (0 occurrences), so the fold is the only evidence for the pointer.

fields.name: type_or_kind
fields.role: written 2 — the only word in the block that says what kind of block it is

fields.name: flags_or_zero
fields.role: written zero; nothing in the block reads it back on the CPU side

fields.name: pair_a_pointer
fields.role: a pointer whose 0xd0-byte extent is CPU-shaped MIPS, not RSP code (see evidence E2): the role is recorded, not named

fields.name: pair_a_size
fields.role: the first pair's size, folded as 0x80028b50 - 0x80028a80 = 0xd0 rather than stored as a constant

fields.name: ucode_pointer
fields.role: this blob: the RSP program the task runs

fields.name: ucode_size
fields.role: the blob's size, exactly IMEM's capacity

fields.name: data_pointer
fields.role: a 0x800-byte region at 0x80136b50 that no other stage-2 instruction names (0 references measured), and whose last 0x5c0 bytes run past the image's end (0x80136d90) into memory this image does not contain

fields.name: list_pointer
fields.role: a value loaded from 0x80143f50, not a constant: the pointer the work list is published through

fields.name: frame_count
fields.role: a halfword loaded through 0x80143f54: the count of work units in that list. Its store sits in the delay slot of the flush call at 0x800a2ed4, so the count and the flush are published in one instruction pair

submitted_to.argument: a0 = the block address, set in the delay slot at 0x800a2ee8 (addu a0,s0,zero)
submitted_to.cache_flush: between the stores and the submit, 0x800a2ed8 calls 0x8000efa0 with (list, count*0xa10): the recipe at 0x800a2eb0-0x800a2ec0 is `sll a1,a2,2 / addu a1,a1,a2 / sll a1,a1,5 / addu a1,a1,a2 / sll a1,a1,4`, i.e. 0xa10 bytes per work unit, which is the manual's requirement that the task header be written back before the RSP reads it (p47)
submitted_to.handler: *(0x80143ff0) — a function pointer, installed by FUN_800b1fc0 (0x800b1fc0:14 `_DAT_80143ff0 = *param_1;`), so the submit path is whatever the driver installed and not a named OS entry point

task.written_by: src/stage2/FUN_800a2e40.c (the corpus's only reference to the block); every store is re-decoded here and its base folded

vector_census.reading: The arithmetic is a 16-bit fixed-point multiply-accumulate pipeline: 48 words multiply and 68 accumulate the product, in the formats the cited table names, and 10 read the accumulator back out. Saturating is not a separate instruction — the multiply opcodes clamp on extraction (cited) — so the mixer's headroom is decided by which format it picks per stage, which is exactly what the counts above report. This says what the units compute; it does not say what the mixer does with the result.
